narrative.overview:
Every question is the index card in the host's hand: question on the front, answer on the back. The interface is a near-black bar top with cards laid on it, and nothing else competes with the card. On the host view one card fills the deck and the next two cards wait behind it.

The material is muted dark stock: six tints (ochre, sage, slate, dusk rose, rust, and brick for the Final), each with a light ink in the same hue, faint blue ruling every baseline sits on and a muted red header rule. One typeface, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, for legibility at arm's length in low light. The presenter screen is plain text on the ground, not a card.
keyCharacteristics: One near-black ground; colour lives on the cards, never on the page.
Stock colour is the wayfinding: round tabs, card ink, the Flip button and primary actions all take the current round's stock.
Ruling and header rule are card furniture, present on every card including forms and sign-in.
One typeface, one icon set (Lucide, inlined), pill buttons, 10px cards.
The answer is on the back of the card, and on the presenter screen it does not exist in the markup until the host reveals it.

rules.name: The Stock Is the Round Rule
rules.body: A round's colour is its stock, and the same stock tints its tabs, its cards, and the primary button while its card is showing. Do not introduce a colour for state; use stock ink, or Warning Coral for danger.

rules.name: The Colour Lives on Cards Rule
rules.body: The ground and chrome stay neutral. Colour appears on cards and on things that belong to a card.

rules.name: The Ruled Line Rule
rules.body: Text on a card sits on the ruling: card line pitch (--lh) is 2rem, 2.5rem on the host deck at 48rem and up, and body lines inside a card take that pitch.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: One family. Hierarchy comes from size, weight and ink, not a second typeface.

rules.name: The Real Hand Rule
rules.body: Depth on the deck is the actual next cards, not a drawn edge or a bigger shadow. Never more than two behind.

dos: Do set every card header as a ruled line: label left, points or context right, 2px Header Red beneath.
Do colour by stock: use the round's stock for tabs, card ink and the primary action on that card.
Do keep text on the ruling by using the card line pitch (2rem, 2.5rem on the wide deck).
Do keep action rows on the unruled foot of the card.
Do confirm permanent actions (Ban) and keep them apart from reversible ones (Swap).
Do keep the answer out of the presenter markup until the host reveals it.
Do give every flip and deal a reduced-motion crossfade alternative.
Do use Lucide icons from src/icons.ts and the single typeface.
donts: Don't replace the card with a row, a disclosure arrow, or a scrolling list on the host view.
Don't put an eyebrow or small label above a heading; the header rule carries that information.
Don't colour the ground or the page chrome with stock colours; they belong to cards.
Don't use Header Red for anything but the card header rule and the revealed-answer rule.
Don't add a second typeface or a glyph or emoji in place of an icon.
Don't draw fake card edges; the cards behind are the real next cards.
Don't shrink tab hit areas to the visible tab; they extend across the gaps.
